rationale: The candidate reads as a compact carved mass with some site response, but it is not yet a convincing neighborhood-living object. Across the four views the form is legible, yet the dominant gesture is unstable: the top view suggests a rotated wedge with a central opening, while the elevations read as a mostly tapered slab with a clipped upper condition. The shape does respond somewhat to the parcel and does keep within it, but the open-space figure is weak and the access edge is not clearly activated; the frontage remains more sealed than public. Program-wise, this feels closer to a sculpted pavilion or generic carved object than a street-facing mixed-use neighborhood building with an active ground threshold. The stepped/terraced language is present but not yet program-bearing enough to compensate for the weak court, weak hierarchy, and limited street articulation.
